newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse seen dependent on dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse seen dependent on dollar strength.

text.p: The direction of German shares was expected to be dependent on the strength of the dollar and movements on Wall Street this week, after the market rose to new record highs on Tuesday.

The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day trade in the DAX index of 30 leading shares, ended up 8.10 points at 2,808.62, paring about ten points in late dealings as the dollar slipped lower and Wall Street reversed early gains and fell into negative territory.
The DAX index had ended bourse dealings at 2,810.64 points spurred on by an overnight Wall Street record and dollar gains.

Dealers said the stronger dollar, which pulled above the 1.52 mark level late on Monday and continued to climb on Tuesday, was helping the chemical and auto sectors in particular, both of which are export-oriented and benefit from a weaker mark.
On Tuesday afternoon, the dollar attempted to breach the 1.53 mark level, before falling back under 1.525 marks.

In the car sector, BMW and Daimler-Benz stocks both charged ahead to record highs. BMW shares hit a year high of 995.25, before profit-taking brought the stock back to 981.10 marks, still up 15.60 on Monday's IBIS close.
Meanwhile, Daimler shares reached an all-time high of 100.75 marks in computer dealings, but then pared gains to end up 50 pfennigs at 99.75 marks.
Amongst the chemical companies, BASF AG, Hoechst AG and Bayer AG all reached new year highs encouraging the rest of the market.

Meanwhile, shares in troubled construction firm Philipp Holzmann took a tumble, falling 19 marks, or almost five percent, to 367 marks, after Deutsche Morgan Grenfell raised its loss forecast for the firm.
